Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can get a scoped estimate over to procurement: 

Call highlights (very terse)
- Primary workload: anonymized transaction enrichment + customer-facing insights (chat + batch embeddings)
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~2.5M – 4.5M
- Peak monthly tokens (seasonal spikes): up to ~8M in peak months
- Residency requirement: EU-only for any records containing EU PII; other data can stay in US region
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a budget band rather than exact $/1M — said you were aiming for something in the low-to-mid $1k/1M range for EU-hosted.

As agreed, to give you a clean comparison we need two confirmations from your side:
1) Confirm the steady / peak monthly token ranges above (or correct them).
2) Confirm the procurement target $/1M tokens (if you have a ceiling / preferred band for negotiation).

Notes about regional delta (quick context)
- If EU residency is required for the PII subset, we typically add a regional premium driven by dedicated EU GPU pools, additional compliance controls (KMS in-region, audit log retention), and EU egress/replication costs. Ballpark: 25–40% uplift vs. US-hosted baseline depending on volume and commit length.

I’ve attached a first-pass pricing workbook (RWI-pricing-estimate-2026.xlsx) and our SOC2 evidence summary for procurement to review. I’ll put together a simple $/1M breakout once you confirm the ranges so you have a line-item to take to budget owners.

Next steps / proposed cadence
- You confirm the numbers above (reply inline) — I’ll return a short pricing breakout for US vs EU hosted and two committed reserved options (6m / 12m).
- If that looks good, we schedule a 30-min procurement handoff (legal + finance) and I’ll route the DocuSign SOW + payment terms.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers inline: 

Steady / peak volumes:
- Steady: we expect roughly 3.0M tokens/month to start, ramping to ~4.2M within 3–4 months as we onboard additional clients.
- Peak: our busiest months could reach ~7.5M tokens but those are relatively infrequent.

Residency:
- EU-only for any data derived from EU customers (PII + transaction-level logs). Non-EU data can be processed in the US.

Budget band / target:
- We’re targeting $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on the SLA and region. Procurement is more likely to sign off closer to the lower half of that band if we have good committed discounts and residency assurances.

Two quick clarifying questions before you price it out: 
1) How are you computing the 25–40% EU uplift? Is that primarily infra + egress or are there line items for compliance / logging we should expect to see separately?
2) For reserved capacity (6m / 12m), what typical discounts do you give and how quickly can you turn up dedicated EU pools?

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to get preliminary numbers in this week and have a procurement review next Thursday. If you can get back with a short $/1M breakdown (hosted US, hosted EU, dedicated 12m commit US/EU) that would be ideal.

Elena

Hi Elena — quick breakdown below (numbers are rounded to be procurement-friendly; see attached workbook for line-item math).

Assumptions (baseline)
- Baseline US-hosted (standard shared pool, on-demand): $0.0006 per token = $600 per 1M tokens

Host pricing (no commit)
- US-hosted (on-demand): $600 / 1M tokens
- EU-hosted (on-demand, residency premium estimated at +35%): $810 / 1M tokens

Reserved / Dedicated pricing (example discounts)
- 6‑month commit (reserved capacity): ~12% discount vs on-demand
- 12‑month commit (reserved capacity): ~22% discount vs on-demand

Using your steady ranges (3.0M – 4.2M) here are three short scenarios (rounded):
1) On-demand, US-only processing (3.0M): 3 * $600 = $1,800 monthly; peak months scale accordingly
2) On-demand, mixed (PII routed to EU; rest US) — blended unit cost approximates: ((PII % * EU $/1M) + (rest % * US $/1M)) — we can model this precisely in the workbook if you provide % of tokens that must be EU-resident (estimate?)
3) 12m reserved, full EU-hosted for PII subset (example): US reserved unit ≈ $468 / 1M; EU reserved unit ≈ $631 / 1M

Why EU premium is 25–40% (line items)
- In-region GPU capacity and capacity fragmentation (we reserve pools specifically to guarantee residency)
- In-region KMS and stronger key isolation controls (HSM + additional audit)
- Extended log retention in-region and additional replication/egress avoidance work
- Operational on-call and compliance review cycles for EU data flows

Next steps (short):
- Please confirm the approximate % of tokens that will be routed to EU-resident processing (PII fraction). A quick estimate (e.g., 20% EU-resident) lets me produce a blended $/1M for your steady state.
- If procurement wants committed pricing, I’ll generate a 12m reserved quote (I can include a sample SOW + DocuSign link).
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min procurement handoff (legal + finance) — I’m prepping a one-page that shows on-demand vs 12m reserved for both regions.

I’ve also added a ballpark example inside the attached workbook so procurement sees line-by-line math. If that looks reasonable I can push a formal quote and a DocuSign SOW today.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachments referenced: RWI-pricing-estimate-2026.xlsx (includes on-demand vs reserved breakouts)
